# OfficeHQ

A full-stack office-management web application.

- **Front end:** Angular single-page app (standalone components, lazy routes), built into
  `src/main/resources/static`.
- **Back end:** Spring Boot with Spring MVC `@RestController` endpoints, on an in-memory H2 database
  with Flyway migrations run on boot.

## Build and run

```
bin/build              # build the SPA and package one runnable jar
PORT=3000 bin/start    # start the app (serves the SPA + REST on $PORT)
bin/stop               # stop it
```

Readiness: `GET /actuator/health`.

## Tests

End-to-end tests use Playwright (in `e2e/`) and bind to `data-testid`:

```
bin/e2e                # build, start, run the specs in e2e/specs, then stop
```

# Test launch only (bin/start): include the reason in error bodies, so a refused /__test__/seed
# names the field it cannot store.
spring.web.error.include-message=always
# Spring Boot host config. H2 in-memory in the same JVM; Flyway migrates the schema up on boot from
# db/migration; Actuator health is the readiness probe.

# In-memory H2 (dies with the JVM = clean per-run reset).
spring.datasource.url=jdbc:h2:mem:officehq;DB_CLOSE_DELAY=-1
spring.datasource.driver-class-name=org.h2.Driver
spring.datasource.username=sa
spring.datasource.password=

# Flyway owns the schema (base has no domain migrations). JPA does not create tables.
spring.flyway.enabled=true
spring.jpa.hibernate.ddl-auto=none
# Close the persistence context at the end of the request, not during view rendering.
spring.jpa.open-in-view=false

# Readiness probe.
management.endpoints.web.exposure.include=health
management.endpoint.health.probes.enabled=true

# The SPA is served from src/main/resources/static (built there by bin/build); deep-link
# fallback is in SpaConfig.java.

# Audit sink: one record per line to this known file, so tests assert side-effects by reading it.
# bin/start passes an absolute path via AUDIT_FILE; default is .run/audit.log.
app.audit.file=${AUDIT_FILE:.run/audit.log}
package net.officefloor.hq.app;

import java.io.IOException;
import java.io.UncheckedIOException;
import java.nio.charset.StandardCharsets;
import java.nio.file.Files;
import java.nio.file.Path;
import java.nio.file.StandardOpenOption;
import org.springframework.beans.factory.annotation.Value;
import org.springframework.stereotype.Service;

/**
 * Audit sink: appends one record per line to a KNOWN FILE (app.audit.file, default .run/audit.log)
 * so tests can assert side-effects by reading that file — the second test-assertion channel
 * alongside the UI. The file path + one-record-per-line format is a stable contract, like
 * data-testid: features may be rewritten as long as they keep emitting the agreed records.
 *
 * Inject this bean into any feature that must record an audit entry. Each write flushes (append +
 * SYNC) so a test reads the record immediately.
 */
@Service
public class Audit {

    private final Path file;

    public Audit(@Value("${app.audit.file:.run/audit.log}") String path) {
        this.file = Path.of(path);
    }

    /** Append one audit record. Tests assert the exact line(s) in the file. */
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Build, start the whole app, run the Playwright specs present in e2e/specs, then stop.
set -euo pipefail
cd "$(dirname "$0")/.."

export PORT="${PORT:-3000}"
export BASE_URL="http://localhost:${PORT}"
# Known audit file, shared by the app (bin/start) and the specs (support/audit.ts). Absolute.
export AUDIT_FILE="${AUDIT_FILE:-$PWD/.run/audit.log}"

bin/build
bin/start
cleanup() { bin/stop || true; }
trap cleanup EXIT

# Wait for readiness (Actuator health), then run the Playwright specs against BASE_URL.
for i in $(seq 1 60); do
  if curl -fsS "${BASE_URL}/actuator/health" >/dev/null 2>&1; then break; fi
  sleep 1
done

# Install deps + the Chromium browser (both cached after first run), then run the specs.
( cd e2e && npm ci --silent && npx --yes playwright install chromium && npx playwright test )

content.text:
Clients are now checked before they're saved. If something is wrong, the form says what and nothing is added. `bin/e2e` passes all 3 tests. I also sent requests straight to the server: it refuses a bad entry with a clear message and accepts a good one.

**The rules**
- **Name is required.** A name of only spaces counts as empty.
- **The email must look like `name@company.com`.** It needs a mailbox, an `@`, and a company name followed by at least one `.something`. So `sam@initech` (nothing after the company name), `sam.initech.example` (no `@`) and an empty email are all refused.
- **No shared emails, ignoring capitals.** `OPS@Acme.example` is refused when a client already has `ops@acme.example`. A different mailbox at the same company, like `finance@acme.example`, is fine.

**Where the checks happen**
- **The form** checks all three rules before it sends anything. It shows a specific message, such as "Enter a proper email address, like name@company.com." or "Another client already has the email OPS@Acme.example."
- **The server** checks the same rules again, so they can't be bypassed by calling it directly. A missing name or bad email comes back as a 400 error and a duplicate email as a 409. The form shows the server's message whenever the server refuses a client.

The duplicate check is in the code only; the database itself doesn't forbid two clients with the same email. If two people add the same email at exactly the same moment, both could get through. I didn't add the database rule because it could reject older test data that already has repeated emails. It can be added if you want that guarantee.

The server changes are in `ClientController.java`, `ClientService.java` and `ClientRepository.java`, plus two new files, `ClientErrors.java` and `ClientRejectedException.java`. The form change is in `features/clients/clients.ts`.
